questions.question: What kind of tool is React?
options: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces
A complete web framework with built-in routing and data fetching
A CSS framework for styling pages
A database query language
questions.explanation: React is a library focused on describing UI. Routing, data fetching and project structure are left to you or to frameworks such as Next.js that build on top of React.

questions.question: What does it mean that React is declarative?
options: You write the exact DOM steps needed to update the page
You describe what the UI should look like for the current data and React works out the updates
You declare all variables before using them
You must declare every component in a central registry
questions.explanation: Declarative means you describe the result. React compares your description with the previous one and applies the necessary DOM changes itself.

questions.question: What does a piece of JSX actually produce when it runs?
options: A real DOM node inserted into the page
A plain JavaScript object describing the intended UI
An HTML string that is parsed later
A CSS rule
questions.explanation: JSX compiles to calls that return plain objects - React elements - with a type and props. React uses those objects to decide what real DOM changes to make.

questions.question: When a component's state changes, what does React do with the component function?
options: It patches only the changed line of the function
It calls the whole component function again and diffs the result
It never calls the function again after the first render
It reloads the page
questions.explanation: React re-runs the entire component function to get a fresh element tree, then applies only the differences to the real DOM. Minimal work happens in the DOM, not in the function call.

questions.question: Why must a component name start with a capital letter?
options: It is only a style convention with no effect
JSX treats lowercase tags as HTML elements and capitalised tags as components
React refuses to compile lowercase functions
Lowercase names are reserved for hooks
questions.explanation: JSX uses the case of the tag to decide its meaning. `<welcome />` is compiled as a literal HTML tag named welcome, while `<Welcome />` refers to the component in scope.

questions.question: Write a component that renders a heading
questions.explanation: A component is a capitalised function returning JSX, and it appears on screen only when something renders it.
